Subject: Model fit & JSON-output evals — next steps

Hi Samantha / Kyle —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + next steps from our discovery and the initial evals we ran on the sample prompts you shared. TL;DR: we have a recommended starting configuration and a short A/B plan to validate JSON-schema compliance for your structured outputs.

What we heard
- Primary endpoint: generate structured product metadata from customer-upload CSV (title, category, cleaned_description, specs JSON).
- Success criteria: >=95% schema compliance on required fields, average latency < 350ms p95, and maintain semantic quality (no hallucinated specs).

Initial recommendations (what we ran in the sandbox)
- Recommended models to trial: Redwood-40B-quant (fp16+INT4 path) and Redwood-7B-refined for cheap fallbacks.
- Mode: function-calling / structured output mode with schema enforcement in the eval harness. We include a schema strictness flag to treat missing required fields as failures so we can measure compliance precisely.
- Observed results (attached CSV): Redwood-40B-quant: schema_pass 92% baseline; Redwood-7B-refined: schema_pass 78% baseline. Typical failures: missing optional nested fields, wrong numeric types in specs, and occasional truncated JSON on token limits.

Tool / function-calling notes
- We ran the structured-output evaluator that validates payloads against the provided JSON Schema and attempts one auto-repair retry (same prompt + small system hint to 'fill missing fields' with exponential backoff). Auto-repair improved pass rates by ~4-6% on the 40B trial.
- For retries we recommend idempotent retries with deterministic prompt patches (e.g., add: "If any required fields are missing, populate with "null" or empty array rather than free-text"). See sample_schema_retry_tests.json attachment for examples.

Ask / next steps
1) Confirm you’re OK with Redwood-40B-quant as the primary eval model and Redwood-7B-refined as a cost-tier fallback.
2) Share a 200–500 record validation set (anonymized) for a run with your internal success metrics.
3) Book a 30-minute technical review with Aditya to walk through the schema edge cases and retry logic.
4) If you want, we can also run a latency-optimized profile (smaller context window + streaming) to target p95 < 350ms.

Links & attachments
- Benchmark CSV: acme_benchmark_results_20260511.csv (attached)
- Prompt sets: acme_prompt_sets_v1.json (attached)
- Benchmarks: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/acme-retail-2026

Happy to adjust the plan based on your priorities — next best step is the shared validation set + the technical deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Hi Samantha — great questions, answers below.

1) Schema pass metric: the 92% is the baseline after one automatic repair attempt (i.e., original generation + one auto-repair pass). Unrepaired baseline (no retry) was ~88%. For GA we typically target >=95% depending on downstream tolerance; for Acme’s use-case (catalog ingestion) I recommend a target of 95%+ on required-field presence and type correctness, with quality gates for hallucinated spec values (see #3).

2) Latency: in our sandbox (eu-west hardware) Redwood-40B-quant observed p50 ~120ms, p95 ~330ms for a 512-token context with streaming disabled. With a small-context profile (truncate to 256 tokens + streaming) we can push p95 below 250ms. Exact numbers depend on your incoming prompt size and whether you enable streaming. We’ll instrument your validation run and report p50/p95/p99.

3) Retry / hallucination risk: the auto-repair retry uses constrained instructions (not free-text heuristics). By default we: 
  - prefer filling missing required fields with a deterministic sentinel (null / empty array) when content is unknown,
  - only attempt to synthesize values where we have high-confidence markers in the prompt (e.g., SKU patterns).
In our experiments with your prompts, the repair that "filled in" values did so in <2% of failures; most repairs simply added empty/null placeholders. We include an explicit audit flag so you can see when a field was auto-populated. If you prefer, we can set the repair policy to "no-synthesize" which will treat any filled-in synthetic value as a hard failure instead.

Attachments & examples
- Attached: sample_schema_retry_tests.json (contains examples of failed payloads, repair prompt templates, and pass/fail labels).
- Attached: acme_benchmark_results_20260511.csv (full results and per-case notes).

Next step proposal
- I'll schedule a 30-min tech review with Aditya. Aditya — can you run through a short checklist in that call: schema edge-cases, tokenization/truncation safeguards, and the repair templates we used?
- Samantha / Kyle: if you can drop the anonymized 200-record set in the Drive link, we’ll queue a full run and share a pass/fail report + logs within 48 hours.

If that works I’ll get invites out.

Best,
Marissa
